title: The information two signals share: mutual information (a newly-authored op), bit-for-bit against sklearn

dataset.name: BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset
dataset.record: subject bidmc01, RESP + PLETH decimated 125->25 Hz, 200 s (5001 samples each)
dataset.citation: Pimentel MAF et al. Toward a robust estimation of respiratory rate from pulse oximeters. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2017;64(8):1914-1923. BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: Transfer entropy (the sibling case) measured the DIRECTED coupling of respiration and pulse; mutual information measures the UNDIRECTED, symmetric dependence -- how much information the two signals share, capturing any (nonlinear) statistical relationship. The ecosystem had directed TE, coherence, cross-correlation, and distance correlation, but no general mutual-information op; this case introduces a NEWLY-AUTHORED op, mutualInformation. On real cardiorespiratory signals it reproduces sklearn.metrics.mutual_info_score BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~5e-16) on the identical binning, and it detects the coupling: the real RESP-PLETH mutual information (0.077 nats) is ~3.2x the histogram estimator's shuffled finite-sample floor (0.024) -- a genuine undirected dependence, the respiratory modulation shared by the two signals.

claims.statement: mutual information of RESP and PLETH (histogram estimator, nats) -- the undirected shared information
sklearn.metrics.mutual_info_score on the identical binning -- matches the op
mutual information of RESP vs a SHUFFLED PLETH -- the histogram estimator's finite-sample bias floor
real / shuffled MI ratio -- the coupling detected above the finite-sample floor
samples per signal (200 s at 25 Hz)

validation.reference: The newly-authored mutualInformation op is validated against sklearn.metrics.mutual_info_score. sklearn re-computes the mutual information from the contingency table of the identical equal-width bin labels; the agreement is BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~5e-16) because both compute I = sum p(x,y) log[p(x,y)/(p(x)p(y))] in nats on the same binning. A seeded shuffled-surrogate control quantifies the histogram estimator's finite-sample bias: the real MI (0.077 nats) is ~3.2x the shuffled floor (0.024).
validation.data: REAL -- BIDMC (PhysioNet), subject bidmc01, RESP + PLETH decimated to 25 Hz, 200 s
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the newly-authored mutualInformation reproduces sklearn.metrics.mutual_info_score bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~5e-16); (2) the real RESP-PLETH MI (0.077 nats) is ~3.2x a shuffled-surrogate floor (0.024). HONEST scope: (1) this op is NEWLY AUTHORED to fill a gap -- the ecosystem had directed transfer entropy, coherence, cross-correlation, and distance correlation, but no general mutual-information op; (2) this is a genuine MACHINE-PRECISION match -- the op and sklearn compute the IDENTICAL contingency-table MI in nats on the same equal-width binning, so the ~5e-16 residual is the floating-point floor, not a convention agreement; (3) this is the HISTOGRAM estimator, which has a POSITIVE finite-sample bias -- the shuffled surrogate (0.024 nats, not 0) quantifies it, and the reproducible finding is that the real dependence (0.077) is ~3.2x ABOVE that floor, NOT the absolute MI value; the KSG/kNN estimator is a less-biased alternative; the MI is in nats (natural log); (4) MI is instantaneous and undirected -- the model-free UNDIRECTED complement of the transfer-entropy fold on the SAME pair; single subject, 200 s; run_simulation = FALSE (the shuffle control is seeded).

open_questions.q: The histogram estimator is bin-count-dependent and positively biased; the KSG/kNN estimator (Kraskov 2004) is less biased and bin-free. Implementing a KSG mutualInformation -- and computing a bias-corrected effective MI (real minus shuffled) across a cohort -- would give an absolute, comparable dependence measure to pair with the directed transfer entropy. Documented, not escalated.
